name: Kristen Michal
role: Prime Minister of the Republic of Estonia (peaminister)
party: Eesti Reformierakond (Estonian Reform Party, RE) — Renew Europe
bio: Kristen Michal, born in Tallinn in 1975 and a law graduate of Akadeemia Nord, has been Prime Minister of Estonia since 23 July 2024 and chairman of the Estonian Reform Party since 8 September 2024. A party member since 1996, he rose from adviser posts to Reform's secretary general (2003–2011) and served as Minister of Justice (2011–2012), resigning in December 2012 after the 'Silvergate' party-financing affair, in which prosecutors had named him a suspect before closing the case without charges; he was later Minister of Economic Affairs and Infrastructure (2015–2016) and Minister of Climate (2023–2024). He succeeded Kaja Kallas when she became the EU's foreign policy chief, at the head of a Reform–Estonia 200–Social Democratic coalition that raised VAT and planned a temporary security tax; in March 2025 he expelled the Social Democrats, and the remaining Reform–Estonia 200 government dropped most of the planned tax rises, abolished the 'tax hump' from 2026, passed a constitutional amendment ending local voting rights for third-country nationals and planned defence spending of about 5.4% of GDP for 2026. As of October 2026 he leads a minority government: the coalition lost its majority in August 2026 when two MPs left their parties, Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur resigned in September over a failed €70 million ammunition procurement for Ukraine, and an opposition motion of no confidence failed in October 2026 with 34 votes after the Social Democrats abstained. Polls in 2025–2026 put his job approval at around one in five voters ahead of the Riigikogu election due on 7 March 2027.
